text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Fenerbahce writes history. The Turkish soccer champions beat Manchester United in England in the European champions' league -- United's first home defeat in 40 years in European competition.
- Interior minister said police should have handcuffed a suspected rebel Kurd suicide bomber who, her hands free, went on to blow up herself and four others after being taken into custody.
- Turkish chief of staff said the army could finish off the rebel Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) in three months if it were not to respect democracy, human rights and legal principles.
- The transport ministry is planning to have a tunnel built under the Bosphorus strait that divides Istanbul to help solve traffic congestion on the two bridges over the waterway.
- World bank officials are coming to Turkey to monitor the spending of $100 million credit they secured for Ankara's privatisation projects.
- The United States warns rival Iraqi Kurdish groups that it will withdraw from peace talks in Ankara if the warring factions fail to come to an agreement.
- Turkish union of chambers and trade bourses warns Islamist prime minister Necmettin Erbakan against pursuing populist policies that could damage the economy.
- The government is going to set up an undersecretariat to investigate claims of human rights abuses.
- Finally a new law increases fines for bad driving that kills thousands of people on Turkey's roads each year.
